messages:
ops-oncall: starting a thread — we're shifting traffic off eu-west because GPU pools are degraded (OOM storms on p3s). initiated DNS failover 1925000000, set new A records pointing to us-west LB with TTL=10s, but seeing ~30–90s propagation to some customers. partial 503 spike from asia edges.

maria: timeline pls — did we change authoritative NS or just A records?

ops-oncall: only A records in our primary zone (route53). did NOT change NS. registrar TTL is standard. route53 change pushed immediately but some resolvers still returning old addresses.

jia: dig +short @8.8.8.8 service.redwood-inference.com -> still returns eu-west IP for me (cached). did you set ALIAS or CNAME?

ops-oncall: ALIAS to elb-us-west-1. TTL in route53 was 10s when we pushed. I suspect intermediate resolver caches + some corporate resolvers honoring previous TTLs.

nic: is this purely DNS? could backend health checks be failing on the us-west LB causing 503s even after DNS flips?

ekaterina: checked LB health — green. logs show successful connections but increased latency on warm-up for some model shards. not 503 at LB layer, 503s appear at edge proxies that still send traffic to eu-west and then get blackholed.

infra-bot: incident: GPU pool eu-west-1a degraded — 40% capacity lost, autoscaler suppressed due to quota limit. Ticket #INF-4721 created.

sre-lead: quick mitigation options: 1) lower TTL to 5s (if resolvers comply), 2) create short-lived CNAME to us-west from a different hostname and rotate client configs, 3) BGP/Anycast steer at CDN level if available.

maria: we can't rely on resolver compliance. recommend dual approach: keep pushing DNS and also put an HTTP 302 from eu-west endpoints to us-west for client redirects while we drain eu-west.

jia: 302s only help for HTTP clients. grpc/embeddings SDKs won't follow. We need source-level routing fallback in the edge layer. Can we enable fallback route at the edge for requests hitting eu-west?

ops-oncall: edge team says they can enable 'prefer-local=false' fallback to route to us-west if local model cache miss occurs. enabling now.

nic: also, for TTL tuning — some corporate resolvers clamp TTL to >=60s. longer-term we should document that in runbooks and use BGP/HTTP steer when sub-60s cutover is required.

ekaterina: started a small script to proactively flush public resolver caches via Cloudflare API where possible (for proxied domains). run:

```
# example: Cloudflare purge by host
curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/$ZONE/purge_cache" \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: infra@redwood.com" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"hosts":["service.redwood-inference.com"]}'
```

ops-oncall: good. also running a dig sweep: ``for r in 8.8.8.8 1.1.1.1 9.9.9.9; do dig @$r service.redwood-inference.com +short; done`` — results vary.

maria: action items: (1) keep TTL=10 but add note to runbook about resolvers that clamp TTLs, (2) enable edge fallback (done?), (3) launch redirect for HTTP (we need QA), (4) open support with our CDN provider to request emergency steer and resolver cache flush.

sre-lead: confirm edge fallback enabled?

ops-oncall: enabled at 1925000055, monitoring. early metrics show reduction in 503s from 7% -> 1.8% on affected prefixes.

nic: cost note — routing more traffic to us-west increases on-demand GPU usage and will spike bill for the incident window. estimate +18% for the day. logging that for post-incident review.

jia: significant number of clients still on cached eu-west IPs. can we publish advisory: "If you see failures, flush your resolver cache / restart client" — but don't want to spam customers. Maybe targeted CS outreach for high-SLI customers.

ekaterina: opened CDN emergency request at 1925000088. they acknowledged and queued a BGP steer. ETA 10–12m.

ops-oncall: update: CDN steer applied at 1925000140. monitoring shows most public resolvers now returning us-west. 503s down to 0.6%.

maria: post-incident action: add a preflight checklist for DNS failovers: include registrar constraints, common resolver clamp behavior, CDN steer contacts, preferred TTL minimums, and an emergency fallback routing toggle at edge.

nic: +1 and also add cost estimate step to know whether to accept cross-region spillover.

ops-oncall: incident closed as mitigated at 1925000184. will file postmortem and follow up with runbook updates. Thanks all :party-parrot:
